:::

::: {.why}
You know how to prevent look-ahead in a feature; a pretrained model brings its own look-ahead that no timestamp in your pipeline can catch, and that is a genuinely new failure mode.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the leak precisely: what a pretrained model knows about your backtest period that your features do not.
- Design an experiment that would detect it, and say what result would be evidence of contamination.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Write the argument out: a model trained on text through some date has seen commentary about the outcomes of events in your backtest window, so a sentiment score it produces for a 2019 filing is not a 2019 sentiment score. Your store cannot catch it because the leak is in the weights rather than in the data.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Design the detection experiment: score filings with the model and check whether its apparent skill is higher on well-known events than on obscure ones, or higher on large caps than small, holding the actual predictability constant as far as you can. Then run a version on filings after the model's training cutoff, which is the only genuinely clean test available.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Write the policy for the book: where a language model is the right tool, which is summarising or extracting a structured field from unstructured text, and where it is not, which is producing a judgement about an outcome. Extraction is much harder to contaminate than prediction.
:::
:::

- [Chen, Pelger & Zhu — Deep Learning in Asset Pricing](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00745) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A written statement of the pretrained-model leak with a detection experiment designed, plus the extraction-versus-prediction policy for the book.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Name the leak specific to pretrained models that does not exist when you build your own features, and say why your point-in-time store cannot catch it.
:::
